terms.gloss: a contractor, a purveyor: one who undertakes by contract to build, supply or carry out something
evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 2.4.2: redemptōrī tuō dīmidium pecūniae cūrāvī
terms.comment: The man who has taken a contract (redimere), for a building, for supplies or for collecting a tax; the closest classical word for a firm’s supplier. Christian Latin uses the same word for the Redeemer (Lewis & Short), a sense the context keeps apart. For a single delivery a relative clause is plainer: is quī nōbīs lateres praebet.
Rare: Lewis & Short has it once in Cicero, of those who furnished what visiting officials needed, and once in Ambrose.

phrases.english: I have seen to it that your contractor got half the money
The supplier hasn’t brought the bricks yet.

sources: Lewis & Short: redemptor · Lewis & Short: praebitor · Lewis & Short: redimo
